theme: Behind the Magic: what 72 hours before a corporate event actually looks like

linkedin.text:
Nobody talks about the 72 hours before.

Before 800 delegates walk into a corporate conference and it feels seamless, this is what's happening:

→ Stage geometry rebuilt after sightline check
→ AV failure discovered and resolved at 11pm
→ Lighting redesigned against a brand update received day-of
→ Catering grid reworked for last-minute dietary data
→ Floor plan version 7 printed at 5am

And then the doors open. And none of it is visible.

We've produced 1,500+ events across 130+ destinations since 2010. The thing every single one has in common: the quality of the invisible preparation determines the quality of the visible experience.

For any HR, Sales or Marketing leader currently planning a conference, product launch or incentive program — what's the part of the planning process that concerns you most?

Drop it in the comments. Happy to share how we approach it.

— Catering logistics adjusted for three dietary variations nobody mentioned until Tuesday
— Lighting reprogrammed to match brand guidelines we received at 6am on day two

By the time delegates walk in, none of that exists. There's only the experience.
